scams.name: Pickpocketing
scams.description: Pickpockets in Lyon work the tourist-heavy areas and crowded public transport, usually in teams: one person asks for directions, bumps into you, or stages a scene while the others lift your wallet or phone. At the Confluence tram stop, groups of women carrying oversized bags have been observed surrounding tourists to get at backpacks. On Métro Line D and the T2 tram, thefts cluster around rush-hour boarding and exiting when movement is chaotic enough to mask the lift.
scams.avoidance: Wear bags across your body with zippers facing inward. Keep only minimal cash and one card on you. Use money belts or hidden pouches. Stay alert during metro boarding and exiting.
scams.location: Vieux Lyon, Place Bellecour, Part-Dieu station, Perrache station, Confluence Tram stop, Metro Line D, T2 tram line, Basilica of Notre-Dame de Fourvière

scams.name: Fake Metro Ticket Scam
scams.description: Ticket touts approach tourists who appear lost or confused at major Lyon train stations. They offer to sell metro tickets at seemingly reasonable prices, but the tickets are either fake, expired, or already used. The scammer may claim they have ‘extra’ tickets or offer a ‘discount’ compared to the official ticket machines. When you try to use the ticket, it won’t work at the turnstile.
scams.avoidance: Only buy tickets from official TCL machines or counters. Use the TCL mobile app for digital tickets. Ignore anyone offering to sell tickets outside official channels.

scams.name: Fake Charity/Petition Scam
scams.description: Someone approaches along Rue de la République with a clipboard and opens with ‘Do you speak English?’ They want you to sign a petition for a deaf-mute charity. Once you’ve signed, they flip to a donation column and pressure you for cash — while your attention is on the clipboard, an accomplice is often working your bag from behind. The charity is fake.
scams.avoidance: Simply say ‘Non, merci’ and keep walking. Never sign anything handed to you on the street. Legitimate charities in France only ask for email addresses, not cash.
scams.location: Rue de la République, Part-Dieu station, Perrache station, Place Bellecour

scams.name: Restaurant Overcharging
scams.description: Tourist-centric restaurants near Lyon’s historic areas may present inflated bills. Tactics include: adding items you didn’t order, charging for bread and water that appeared ‘free,’ using ‘tourist menus’ with elevated prices. Some establishments trade on Lyon’s reputation as France’s gastronomic capital to justify excessive prices for mediocre food.
scams.avoidance: Check prices before sitting down. Ask for itemized bills and review carefully. Eat where locals eat, away from main tourist streets.
scams.location: Vieux Lyon (Old Town), Presqu’île, Rue Mercière

scams.name: Shell Game / Three-Card Monte
scams.description: A scammer sets up a makeshift table with three cups or cards. They invite you to bet on guessing the ball’s location. ‘Winners’ in the crowd are accomplices who pretend to win to draw you in. The game is completely rigged through sleight of hand — you cannot win.
scams.avoidance: Never play street gambling games — they are always rigged. Do not stop to watch. Remember that bystanders are likely accomplices.
scams.location: Busy tourist areas, Near major attractions, Metro exits

scams.name: Gold Ring Scam
scams.description: A person ‘finds’ a gold ring on the ground near you and asks if you dropped it. When you say no, they show you a marking claiming it’s real gold and offer to sell it for a ‘good price.’ The ring is worthless brass. They may also ask for money ‘for food’ or ‘for their children.’
scams.avoidance: Don’t engage — say ‘Non’ and keep walking. Never accept items ‘found’ on the street.
scams.location: Tourist walkways, Near bridges, Pedestrian areas

scams.name: Friendship Bracelet Scam
scams.description: A vendor grabs your hand in Vieux Lyon and weaves a colorful string bracelet around your wrist, finishing with a knot you can’t untie. Then they demand €10–€20. If you refuse, they become aggressive — and in the confrontation, an accomplice often works your pockets.
scams.avoidance: Keep your hands in your pockets when approached. Say ‘Non’ firmly and keep walking. Don’t let anyone touch you or attach anything.
scams.location: Tourist attractions, Near churches, Pedestrian areas

scams.name: Rose/Flower Scam
scams.description: A seller approaches couples dining outdoors, offering a rose with ‘Flower for the pretty lady!’ The moment you touch or accept the flower, they demand 5-10 euros. If you try to return it, they refuse and become aggressive until you pay out of embarrassment.
scams.avoidance: Don’t touch or accept any flowers offered. A simple ‘Non, merci’ and wave sends them away. Ask restaurant staff to intervene if needed.
scams.location: Restaurant terraces, Romantic spots, Evening entertainment areas

scams.name: Fake Police Scam
scams.description: Criminals pose as plainclothes police, flash fake badges, and say they need to check your wallet for counterfeit bills or ‘drug money.’ While examining the cash, they palm bills. Sometimes a ‘lost tourist’ accomplice has just asked you to break a large note, and the fake officer arrives moments later claiming street currency exchange is illegal.
scams.avoidance: Real officers only ask to see ID, never the wallet. Ask to see their *carte de police* and offer to walk to the nearest *commissariat* together — genuine police will comply; scammers won’t. Dial 17 if something feels off.
scams.location: Metro stations, Tourist areas, Near bars at night

scams.name: Taxi Overcharging
scams.description: Some taxi drivers take advantage of tourists unfamiliar with Lyon’s layout. They take long routes to inflate the fare, ‘forget’ to start the meter, or select the higher night or weekend tariff during regular hours. Airport runs are particularly vulnerable — the legitimate fare from Lyon-Saint Exupéry to the city center is around €50–€70.
scams.avoidance: Only use taxis from official ranks. Ensure the meter is zeroed before departure. Use GPS on your phone to follow the route. Consider using Uber or Bolt.
scams.location: Lyon-Saint Exupéry Airport, Part-Dieu station, Perrache station, Outside nightclubs

scams.name: ATM Skimming / Private ATM Scam
scams.description: Criminals attach skimming devices to ATMs that steal your card data and PIN. Private ATM companies like Euronet place machines that charge excessive fees and poor exchange rates — up to 4x more than bank ATMs. They may offer Dynamic Currency Conversion at terrible rates.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside bank branches only. Look for major French banks: BNP Paribas, Société Générale, LCL. Always cover keypad when entering PIN. Decline dynamic currency conversion.
scams.location: Private ATMs in tourist areas, ATMs on busy streets, Near train stations

scams.name: Broken Camera Scam
scams.description: Someone asks you to take their photo using their camera. After you return the camera, they claim you broke it and demand money for repairs. The ‘camera’ was already broken — they use it repeatedly for this scam.
scams.avoidance: Politely decline to take photos with others’ cameras. If accused of damage, suggest filing a police report together — scammers will refuse.
